extraction.name: CommonCanvas
extraction.description: An open diffusion model trained with Creative-Commons images. The dataset consists of roughly 70 million Creative-Commons-licensed images with synthetic captions generated using BLIP-2. Two variants are provided: CommonCatalog-C (commercial use, ~26M images) and CommonCatalog-NC (non-commercial use, ~67M images).
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.citeAs: Gokaslan et al. (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825v1 [cs.CV]
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was sourced from YFCC100M, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs. Images were re-scraped from Flickr based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata to obtain high-resolution versions (exceeding 4K). Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. The remaining images were divided into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) categories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YFCC100M dataset consisting of 100 million CC-licensed images from Flickr. Images were re-scraped from Flickr based on Flickr IDs to obtain high-resolution versions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels for captioning. At training time of the diffusion model, all images remain in their native resolution.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. The remaining images were divided into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) categories. Images were re-scraped from Flickr to obtain very high resolution versions (exceeding 4K). For captioning, images were center-cropped and resized to 512x512 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were generated using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model. The BLIP-2 model consists of three components: a pre-trained, frozen visual encoder, a learned transformer network that converts visual embeddings into a text prompt, and a frozen large language model (LLM) that takes in the prompt. All YFCC100M Creative-Commons images were captioned using this approach, requiring about 1,120 GPU A100 hours.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: BLIP-2 captions were found to be qualitatively more descriptive than LAION-2B ground-truth alt-text captions. LAION-2B captions often contain product names, irrelevant details, or poor grammar and syntax. This finding is corroborated by Nguyen et al., which shows quantitatively (in terms of CLIP Score) that BLIP-2 captions are higher quality than ground-truth captions, at the cost of caption diversity.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The commercial (CommonCatalog-C) and non-commercial (CommonCatalog-NC) CC-image and synthetic-caption datasets are released on HuggingFace with associated data cards. BLIP-2 captions for non-derivative (ND) CC images not used for training are also released as an evaluation set.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work addresses copyright concerns in text-to-image generative models by training only on Creative-Commons-licensed data with known provenance. This approach avoids the unclear provenance issues associated with web-scraped datasets like LAION-5B and provides a path forward for future research on highly-capable, open T2I models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The YFCC100M data is about a decade old; its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. The model underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings. Reduced diversity of n-grams was observed in synthetic captions compared to ground-truth captions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: CC images rarely have the alt-text captions necessary to train T2I models. Only roughly 70 million usable CC images could be found, which is significantly less than the billions of images in LAION used to train SD2. The dataset is about a decade old and not as current as LAION-2B. The model underperformed in categories like faces, general photography, and paintings. Synthetic captions exhibit reduced diversity compared to ground-truth captions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image latent diffusion models. The dataset is intended for training high-quality T2I models using only open-licensed, Creative-Commons data. CommonCatalog-C is suitable for commercial applications, while CommonCatalog-NC includes additional non-commercial images.
